Subject: Security questionnaire: eviction/retention timeline + snapshots

Hi Sergio,

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the security questionnaire for our procurement review and have a couple of specific items about the hosted API:

1) If we request a tenant data eviction (complete deletion for an account), what is the expected timeline from request to data being unrecoverable at the hosted-API layer? Please break out hot-cache, primary storage, and backups/snapshots.

2) Do you provide any snapshot export (export of customer-owned data) prior to deletion? If so, what's the workflow and how long does it take? Are exports kept by Redwood or pushed to our storage?

3) How do you handle KV/prefix caches and in-flight requests at deletion time? Does cached context leak after deletion?

4) Any evidence or runbook we can attach to the RFI? (we'll attach the questionnaire spreadsheet).

Appreciate concise answers and any attachments you can share so we can include them in the security packet.

Best,
Maya Singh
Security & Compliance Manager
Atlas Logistics

Hi Maya — thanks for the clear questions. High-level answers below; attaching a short runbook and our evidence pack for the RFI. Happy to hop on a quick call if you prefer.

Summary (short):
- Hot cache (prefix/KV cache): logical eviction occurs immediately on request; keys removed within seconds, and cache-control signals are broadcast across the serving cluster.
- Primary storage (tenant logical deletion): logical deletion propagated within 24 hours in normal operations; physical removal from object store depends on retention/snapshot windows (see backups).
- Backups / snapshots: snapshots are immutable and scheduled; we will schedule an ad-hoc export if you require a tenant snapshot before deletion. Standard backup retention windows mean snapshot artifacts could exist until the next backup lifecycle truncation (up to 72 hours depending on timing).

Answers by question:
1) Timeline by lane:
  - Hot cache: immediate logical eviction; cache entries removed cluster-wide within <30s in typical load patterns.
  - Primary store (logical): request accepted and marked for deletion in the control plane, queued for logical purge and metadata scrub; target: complete logical deletion (no customer-visible records) within 24 hours.
  - Physical/irrecoverable: depends on backup/snapshot windows — see (3). We commit to assist customers in scheduling final physical truncation where contractually required.

2) Snapshot/export workflow:
  - We can perform an on-demand export of tenant data (flattened JSON/NDJSON or S3 export) to a customer-owned S3 bucket or secure transfer link.
  - Typical lead time: 2–48 hours depending on size and whether we need to run a cross-region export. Exports initiated by you are delivered to your storage; we do not retain a copy beyond delivery unless explicitly requested.

3) KV/prefix cache & in-flight requests:
  - In-flight requests referencing cached context are not retroactively served after logical deletion. The eviction signal ensures subsequent requests will miss the cache.
  - We run a short grace window for finishing calls in progress (60–300s) to avoid partial failures; those logs are captured and available in audit. No new cached artifacts are created for tenant after deletion begins.

4) Evidence/runbook: attached: hostedapi-eviction-snapshot-procedure.pdf and redwood-erasure-playbook-v2.docx. Also linking to our shared drive folder HS-AL-4721.

If you need firm contract language for physical deletion timing (e.g., within 48h of request), we can review with Legal/Support and add a one-off clause to the DPA.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Maya — following up with a short, copy-ready paragraph and some detail on worst-case windows. Forwarding Sergio's answers below and adding operational specifics.

Copy-ready statement for questionnaire:
"Redwood Inference processes tenant deletion in three logical stages. Hot-serving caches are invalidated immediately on request and cache entries are removed cluster-wide (typical propagation <30s). The tenant is marked for logical deletion in the control plane and customer-visible data is removed from primary indexes within 24 hours. Physical artifacts stored in scheduled snapshots or backup windows may remain immutable until the next backup truncation cycle; worst-case recoverability from backup artifacts is up to 72 hours depending on the timing of the final backup window. Redwood provides on-demand tenant exports delivered to a customer-owned S3 bucket (checksum and signed transfer log provided), and will cooperate on contractual timelines for physical deletion where required."

Operational details (for your team):
- Worst-case backup retention: 72 hours after an ad-hoc deletion request if a full snapshot coincided with deletion; we will prioritize a manual truncate when contractually requested.
- Export/transfer proof: exports include an MD5/SHA256 checksum and a signed delivery log (timestamped delivery event, operator id). We push events to your supplied S3 bucket and record the transfer event in our audit trail.
- Cache race protections: the eviction path sets a tenant-level write lock and an async broadcast to all serving nodes. Any write attempts that would create new cached artifacts after eviction are rejected. In-flight requests are allowed to finish (up to a short grace window, default 120s) but do not create persistent cache entries.

Attachments: I attached the procedure & playbook Sergio referenced. If Atlas wants a contractual SLA for physical irrecoverability (e.g., guaranteed physical purge within X hours), let us know your preferred X and we'll route to Legal.

— Neha Kapoor
Director, Product Security Operations
Redwood Inference
